content:
Using the eval tool, split this Windows path on the backslash separator
and tell me how many segments it has:

    C:\Users\nthalk\src\app\main.go

Reply with just the number.

Using the eval tool: first compute 41 + 1 and persist the result so a LATER
eval call can read it back. Then, in a SEPARATE eval call, read that
persisted value and double it. Reply with just the final number.

You do not know mcpshell's regex API. Find out what it offers WITHOUT
guessing, then use it to report how many whitespace-separated words are in
the string "alpha beta gamma delta". Reply with just the number.

abs(n: number) — absolute value
  addNode(parent: node|string, type: string, props?: object) — adds a node connected from parent. Edge type defaults to node type
  assert(message: string, condition: any) — fails if condition is falsy
  at(input: array|string, index: number) — element at index (supports negative)
  avg(input: array) — arithmetic mean of an array of numbers
  bool(value: any) — → boolean
  both(input: node|array, type?: string) — follows edges in both directions
  ceil(n: number) — rounds up
  charAt(input: string, index: number) — character at index
  chunk(input: array, size: number) — splits into sub-arrays of size n
  concat(a: array, b: array) — concatenates two arrays
  contains(input: array|string, value: any) — membership test
  countBy(input: array, fn?: (T) => string) — → {key: count}; fn defaults to identity
  difference(a: array, b: array) — elements in a not in b
  endsWith(input: string, suffix: string) — suffix test
  entries(input: object) — object → [[key, value], ...] (JS-compatible)
  every(input: array, fn: (T) => boolean) — true if all elements match
  extendLimit(opts: {steps?: number, timeout?: number, callDepth?: number, outputBytes?: number}) — increases execution limits for this eval. Call before heavy computation
  fail(msg?: string) — throws error
  fill(input: array, value: any, start?: number, end?: number) — fills array with value, returns new array
  filter(input: array|object, fn: (T, index?) => boolean) — keeps elements where fn is truthy; on objects filters entries with (value, key)
  find(input: array, fn: (T) => boolean) — first match or null
  flat(input: array) — flattens one level
  flatMap(input: array, fn: (T) => array) — maps then flattens one level
  floor(n: number) — rounds down
  forEach(input: array, fn: (T, index?) => void) — applies fn to each element, returns null
  fromEntries(input: array) — [[key, value]] or [{key, value}] → object
  groupBy(input: array, fn: (T) => string) — → …[truncated]
The help lists the regex API: `match`, `test`, `replace`, and `split` with a regex separator. Using `split` with a whitespace regex:
ERROR: mcp tool error: [ERROR: 's' is already declared in this scope]
{"code":"const words = split(ws, /\\s+/).filter(w => w !== \"\")\nreturn len(words)\n","vars":{"ws": "alpha beta gamma delta"}}
